thread.title: Walmart Ditches Alibaba's Alipay For Tencent's WeChat

author: ELAINE LOW
title: Walmart Ditches Alibaba's Alipay For Tencent's WeChat
text:
Walmart ( WMT ) has reportedly inked a deal with Tencent Holdings ' ( TCEHY ) WeChat in western China, ditching Alibaba 's ( BABA ) Alipay, as mobile payments quickly replace cash in the country .
X Telling Reuters that it was a "business decision" to improve customer experience, a Walmart spokesperson said that the mega-retailer will, down the road, "cooperate with more partners to provide payment solutions with more convenience and benefits."
Alibaba, the biggest online retailer in China, also has a No. 1 player in its Alipay system, which is comparable to Apple ( AAPL ) Pay.
The move further positions Walmart on the side of Alibaba's rivals in the country. Walmart doubled its stake in China's second-biggest e-commerce player , JD.com ( JD ), to 10.8% in late 2016. WeChat operator Tencent is JD.com's largest stakeholder. Together, Tencent and JD.com acquired a 12.5% stake in smaller online competitor Vipshop ( VIPS ) in December.

Alibaba sank 4.5%, Tencent lost 3.3%, and JD.com eased 2.7%.

Domestically, Walmart is engaged with its own battle against Amazon and other major retailers, and shares dove over 10% after reporting a fourth quarter that reflected slowing online sales growth.
Walmart's e-commerce head Marc Lore said at retail conference Shoptalk last week that the slowdown had been "largely planned," and reiterated that he would stay on at the company and has committed to five years there.
